name: Tithe statutes
note: The laws that command a tenth, and say whose it is.

name: The temple tax
note: The half-shekel levy for the temple, and the one scene where anyone reasons about paying it.

name: Imperial tax
note: Rome and the empires before it: census, tribute, and whether paying is lawful.

name: Tax collectors
note: The trade, the men who worked it, and how they were treated.

name: Tithing weighed
note: The two woes and a boast, where tithing is set against the weightier matters and found lighter.

name: The Hebrews 7 argument
note: The argument of Hebrews 7: Melchizedek outranks Levi, so the priesthood changes and the law with it.

name: Treasury and alms
note: The temple treasury, and alms given openly or in secret.

name: Debt and its parables
note: What is owed between people, and the parables built on it.

name: Money changers
note: The money changers in the temple, and the tables overturned.

name: Interest forbidden
note: The prohibition on lending at interest to your own, repeated as a test of righteousness.

name: Remission and jubilee
note: The seventh-year remission and the fiftieth-year jubilee: debts cancelled, land returned.

name: Money entrusted
note: Money handed over to be traded with, and the reckoning that follows.

name: Wages withheld
note: Pay owed to a labourer, and the rule that it must not be held overnight.

name: Gleaning and the field's edge
note: The corners of the field and the second pass of the vineyard, left for those with no land.

name: The common purse
note: The Jerusalem community holding property in common, and what happened when someone held back.

name: Pricing a person
note: What a person is worth in shekels: vows, redemption, and thirty pieces of silver.

name: Treasure in heaven
note: Where wealth is stored, and what storing it in heaven is said to cost.

name: Gold, silver and the fire
note: Gold and silver offered, refined, tested by fire, and finally named the wrong medium of ransom.
